title: Giuga
statement: If an integer n≥2 satisfies sum(a^(n−1), a=1,…,n−1)≡−1 (mod n), then n is prime.

counterexample.description: A composite \(n\) satisfying \(\sum_{a=1}^{n-1}a^{\,n-1}\equiv-1\pmod n\). Given the factorization, modular exponentiation or the equivalent divisibility conditions for every prime divisor are cheap and exact.
